about: Famous comets for the comets module. Generated by tools/build-comets.mjs from Celestia comets.ssc, Stellarium ssystem_minor.ini (both GPL-2.0-or-later, see CREDITS.md) and the hand-entered src/modules/comets/catalog.json. Elements: heliocentric (or barycentric) ecliptic J2000, q in AU, angles in degrees, tp and epoch as JD TT. Blocks marked approximate are hand-entered.

display.source: Appearance constants of the procedural coma and tail model (docs/modules/comets.md); not measurements.

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "1P Halley" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "1P Halley" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit to the 1986 apparition: total visual magnitude about +3 in early March 1986 (r 0.8 AU, delta 0.9 AU), as reported in ICQ visual light curves

look.source: Appearance weights (dusty comet with a clear ion tail in 1986 wide-field photographs); procedural

shape.source: Giotto HMC: about 15 x 8 x 8 km (Keller et al. 1986), rounded

comets.name: Comet Encke
comets.apparition: shortest known period of a bright comet (3.3 yr)

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "2P Encke" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "2P Encke" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude 6-7 near perihelion (r 0.34 AU) at delta 1 AU, typical of recent returns

look.source: Appearance weights (gas-rich, almost no visible dust tail); procedural

shape.source: Generic elongated nucleus; radar and light-curve axis ratios are uncertain

comets.name: Comet Pons-Brooks
comets.apparition: 2024 perihelion (seen near the April 2024 total solar eclipse)

elements.source: Hand-entered from the JPL Small-Body Database orbit for the 2024 apparition (perihelion 2024-04-21.13 TT, q 0.781 AU), rounded; not in Celestia comets.ssc

physical.source: Hand-entered: effective radius about 17 km (Ye et al. 2020 estimate), rotation about 57 h (2024 coma-morphology studies); both uncertain

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude 4.5 near the April 2024 perihelion (r 0.78 AU, delta 1.6 AU), outbursts ignored

look.source: Appearance weights (green coma, long ion tail in 2024 photographs); procedural

shape.source: Generic nucleus; the shape is unknown

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "67P Churyumov-Gerasimenko" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "67P Churyumov-Gerasimenko" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude 9 at the November 2021 return (r 1.21 AU, delta 0.42 AU)

look.source: Appearance weights (dusty Jupiter-family comet, faint ion tail); procedural

shape.source: Rosetta OSIRIS: body lobe about 4.1 x 3.3 x 1.8 km, head lobe about 2.6 x 2.3 x 1.8 km (Sierks et al. 2015), as two overlapping ellipsoids

comets.name: Comet Swift-Tuttle
comets.apparition: 1992 perihelion; parent of the Perseid meteors

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "109P Swift-Tuttle" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "109P Swift-Tuttle" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude 5 in November 1992 (r 0.96 AU, delta 1.2 AU)

shape.source: Generic nucleus; the shape is unknown

elements.source: Stellarium ssystem_minor.ini [C_1995O1] (MPC elements of the apparition)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp)" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: peak total visual magnitude about -0.8 around 1997-04-01 (r 0.91 AU, delta 1.36 AU)

look.source: Appearance weights (broad curved dust tail and a separate blue ion tail in 1997 photographs); procedural

shape.source: Generic nucleus; the shape is unknown

comets.name: Comet Hyakutake
comets.apparition: 1996 close approach to Earth (0.10 AU on 25 March 1996)

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 1996 B2 (Hyakutake)" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 1996 B2 (Hyakutake)" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude 0 at the 1996-03-25 close approach (r 1.07 AU, delta 0.10 AU)

look.source: Appearance weights (blue-green gas comet with a very long ion tail, weak dust tail); procedural

shape.source: Generic nucleus; the shape is unknown

comets.name: Comet McNaught
comets.apparition: 2007 perihelion (Great Comet of 2007, 0.17 AU from the Sun)

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 2006 P1 (McNaught)" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 2006 P1 (McNaught)" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude -5 at the 2007-01-12 perihelion (r 0.17 AU, delta 0.82 AU) and -2 a week later

look.source: Appearance weights (enormous fanned dust tail in January 2007 photographs); procedural

shape.source: Generic nucleus; the shape is unknown

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 2020 F3 (NEOWISE)" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements)

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 2020 F3 (NEOWISE)" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude 1 on 2020-07-05 (r 0.30 AU, delta 1.1 AU) and 3.5 on 2020-07-23 (r 0.63 AU, delta 0.69 AU)

look.source: Appearance weights (curved yellow dust tail and a straight blue ion tail in July 2020 photographs); procedural

shape.source: Generic nucleus; the shape is unknown

elements.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 2023 A3 (Tsuchinshan-ATLAS)" (JPL SBDB / Horizons osculating elements). Perihelion time hand-entered (2024-09-27.74 TT, as published by the MPC and JPL): the mean anomaly of the Celestia row puts the passage 9.5 days early

physical.source: Celestia comets.ssc "C 2023 A3 (Tsuchinshan-ATLAS)" (radius, albedo, rotation; see the references in that file)

photometry.source: Hand-entered fit: about magnitude 0.5 in mid-October 2024 (r 0.56 AU, delta 0.47 AU); the forward-scattering peak near 2024-10-09 is not modelled

look.source: Appearance weights (long dust tail in October 2024 photographs); procedural

shape.source: Generic nucleus; the shape is unknown
